usages.titre: The past is linked to now

etapes.texte: A **result** now: I have **already** sent the invoice
It **continues**: she has worked here **for** five years

aparte.texte: yesterday, last week, in 2019, two days ago

etapes.texte: Look for the **time word** in the sentence
**since, for, already, never, yet**: present perfect

phrases.texte: The present perfect.
We form it with have, or has, and the past participle.
I have sent the invoice. She has worked here for years. He has never visited Paris.
The present perfect links the past to now. First, a result: I have already sent the invoice. It is done.
Second, an action that continues: she has worked here for five years, and she still works here.
Third, an experience in your life: he has never visited Paris.
Since goes with a starting point: since Monday, since 2020.
phrases.dit: Since, goes with a starting point: since Monday, since twenty twenty.

phrases.texte: For goes with a duration: for three days, for five years.
phrases.dit: For, goes with a duration: for three days, for five years.

phrases.texte: Now, the big trap. I have seen him yesterday is wrong.
phrases.dit: Now, the big trap. I have seen him yesterday, is wrong.

phrases.texte: Yesterday is a finished time. So we use the simple past: I saw him yesterday.
It is the same with last week, in 2019, or two days ago.
phrases.dit: It is the same with: last week, in twenty nineteen, or two days ago.

phrases.texte: Now, a TOEIC question from Part 5. Ms. Tanaka, blank, for the company since 2015.
phrases.dit: Now, a TOEIC question from Part five. Miz Tanaka, blank, for the company since twenty fifteen.

phrases.texte: A: works. B: worked. C: has worked. D: is working.
phrases.dit: Answer A. works. Answer B. worked. Answer C. has worked. Answer D. is working.

phrases.texte: Which answer is correct?
Look at the time word: since 2015. It is a starting point, and the action continues today.
phrases.dit: Look at the time word: since twenty fifteen. It is a starting point, and the action continues today.

phrases.texte: So A, B and D are wrong. They do not link the past to now.
phrases.dit: So A, B, and D are wrong. They do not link the past to now.

phrases.texte: C is correct: Ms. Tanaka has worked for the company since 2015.
phrases.dit: C is correct: Miz Tanaka has worked for the company since twenty fifteen.

phrases.texte: Remember three steps. One: look for the time word in the sentence.
Two: since, for, already, never and yet go with the present perfect.
Three: yesterday, last week and ago go with the simple past.
Now practise with the questions below.
phrases.dit: Now, practise with the questions below.
